findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the CI coverage check treats command-GROUP arms (e.g. `audit`, `llm`, `workflow`, `config`) and the doc's deliberate exclusions (`help`, no-subcommand), so the 75-arm target and the row-per-arm assertion are unambiguous and stable.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/help/audit.txt shows `audit` is a group: `rebar audit show <id>` and `rebar audit serve` — a single exit-code row flattens two sub-dispatchers
_INTERCEPTS (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:47-74) includes group parents `llm`,`workflow`,`config`,`identity`,`criteria`,`prompt`,`audit` alongside single commands
docs/exit-codes.md:119-120 deliberately EXCLUDES the `help` arm and the no-subcommand overview arm from the table, but the plan's derivation formula does not carve these out
The plan states the union is 'independently re-derived' but does not define the allowed-exclusions set the CI check must honor
findings.finding: The CI-coverage mechanism ("every dispatcher arm has a row", derived from known_subcommands() ∪ _INTERCEPTS) does not specify how it reconciles two facts about that union: several _INTERCEPTS arms are command GROUPS with per-subcommand exit semantics (e.g. `audit show` vs `audit serve`; also `llm`, `workflow`, `config`, `identity`, `criteria`, `prompt`), and the doc deliberately excludes `help` and the no-subcommand overview arm. As written, the check could demand a semantically-hollow single row for a group-parent or count exclusions inconsistently, making the 75 target unstable.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — "Rows exist for all 75 dispatcher arms" / "A CI check asserts every dispatcher arm has a row"
scenarios: The CI check demands a row for `audit`, but `audit show` and `audit serve` have different failure surfaces, so the single row cannot faithfully state one contract
The check fails on `help`/no-subcommand (excluded by the doc today) unless an explicit allowlist is coded, or silently drifts if the allowlist is hand-maintained separately from the doc
findings.suggested_fix: State the exact expected-arm set in the plan: `known_subcommands() ∪ _INTERCEPTS` MINUS an explicit, doc-anchored exclusion list (help + overview), and decide whether group parents get one row documenting the shared contract or are expanded per leaf-subcommand. Have the CI check read that same exclusion list so the doc and the test cannot drift.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the meaning (or a source symbol/dispatcher arm) for exit codes 3, 4 and 12 so the doc can be written without guesswork
evidence: AC2: 'Codes 3, 4, 12, 75 and 78 are documented with their meanings'
Body: 'Codes 3, 4, 12 ... are also undocumented' — states they are undocumented but gives no meanings
Contrast: 75 and 78 are given explicit source symbols and seam locations
findings.finding: AC2 requires codes 3, 4, and 12 to be documented 'with their meanings', but the plan supplies no meaning or source symbol/location for them (unlike 75=RebaseGuard/EXIT_RESCHEDULE and 78=StoreIncompatibleError which are grounded). The executor must independently investigate what 3, 4, 12 signify.
scenarios: Executor guesses or mis-attributes the meaning of exit code 3/4/12 and documents it incorrectly
findings.suggested_fix: For each of 3, 4, 12, cite where the code is produced (as done for 75/78) or state its meaning directly in the plan.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: No file_impact declared on a leaf work ticket.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the {path, reason} files this work will touch (e.g. via set_file_impact) so the attestation is scoped to them.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether/how the CI check (or a note) guards the code-meanings section (75/78/3/4/12) against future staleness, or document that only rows are machine-enforced and code meanings rely on the conformance test
evidence: AC4: 'A CI check asserts every dispatcher arm has a row'
Body: codes 75/78 'reach the process exit status via _seam.py:419 -> _commands/__init__.py:160' — not dispatcher arms
Title: 'Make docs/exit-codes.md complete and keep it that way'
findings.finding: The title's goal ('keep it that way') and the 'keep the code-meanings complete' intent are only enforced for dispatcher-arm ROWS. The CI check in AC4 enumerates dispatcher arms, but codes 75 and 78 reach process exit via the seam and are NOT dispatcher arms — so no conformance check prevents the code-meanings section from regressing/going stale, which is exactly the failure mode the ticket exists to fix.
scenarios: A future refactor removes/renames RebaseGuard or StoreIncompatibleError; the doc's code entry for 75/78 goes stale and CI stays green because the check only inspects dispatcher-arm rows
findings.suggested_fix: Either extend the CI check to assert the presence of the seam-produced codes, or add a sentence acknowledging code meanings are guarded only by the existing conformance test and not by AC4's enumeration.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion covering documentation of validate's 0-4 severity-bucket exit codes, or explicitly drop it from scope
evidence: Body: 'Codes 3, 4, 12 and validate's 0-4 severity bucket are also undocumented.'
AC2 lists '3, 4, 12, 75 and 78' — the validate 0-4 severity bucket is absent from every AC
findings.finding: The body flags that `validate`'s 0-4 severity bucket is currently undocumented, but no acceptance criterion requires documenting it — described work with no covering criterion. AC2 enumerates only 3, 4, 12, 75, 78.
scenarios: Executor completes all ACs and closes the ticket while validate's 0-4 severity mapping remains undocumented, contradicting the stated defect
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AC2 to include validate's 0-4 severity bucket, or move it to an explicit out-of-scope note.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the 75/78 exit-status citation to the real mapping seam `_commands/_seam.py:528-533` (`raise CommandError(..., returncode=getattr(exc, 'returncode', 1))`), with the returncode sources `_store/lock.py:135` (RebaseGuard=75) and `_store/compat.py:73` (StoreIncompatibleError=78).
evidence: _commands/_seam.py:419 is inside the screen_event docstring ('The refusal names the family/field/line and NEVER the value'), not exit-code mapping code
_commands/__init__.py:160 is a comment ('the heavier event-composers (docs/bash-migration.md §4)') above _ARGV_REGISTRY, not exit-code mapping code
Actual mapping verified at _commands/_seam.py:528-533: raise CommandError(str(exc), returncode=getattr(exc, 'returncode', 1))
findings.finding: The plan's line citations for how codes 75/78 reach the process exit status ('_seam.py:419' -> '_commands/__init__.py:160') point to a docstring line and a registry-comment line, not the actual mapping. The real propagation is at _commands/_seam.py:528-533, which catches (StoreError, RebaseGuard, LockTimeout, StoreIncompatibleError) and raises CommandError(returncode=getattr(exc,'returncode',1)); RebaseGuard.returncode=75 (_store/lock.py:135) and StoreIncompatibleError.returncode=78 (_store/compat.py:73). The substantive premise (75/78 reach the exit status and are undocumented) is CORRECT and verified — only the cited coordinates are wrong.
findings.location: Plan body, paragraph 2 ('Grounding found worse: codes 75 ... and 78 ... reach the process exit status via _seam.py:419 -> _commands/__init__.py:160')
scenarios: An implementer follows the cited lines to understand/document the 75/78 semantics and finds unrelated code, risking a wrong or incomplete doc entry
The CI-check author (AC line 4) uses the citations to locate where non-CommandError exit codes originate and misses the getattr(exc,'returncode') propagation, under-scoping the check
findings.suggested_fix: Replace '_seam.py:419 -> _commands/__init__.py:160' with '_commands/_seam.py:528-533 (CommandError propagates exc.returncode), where RebaseGuard.returncode=75 (_store/lock.py:135) and StoreIncompatibleError.returncode=78 (_store/compat.py:73)'.
